actors.name: Javier Milei
actors.role: President of Argentina, Leader of La Libertad Avanza
actors.blurb: Javier Milei remains a dominant figure in global right-wing discourse due to his aggressive economic reforms, diplomatic engagements, and controversial statements. Over the past 48 hours, his government faced significant backlash after the Senate stripped key measures from his reform bill, particularly those easing foreign land ownership. Milei's international tour, including meetings with Spain's King Felipe VI and Colombia's new president, has also drawn attention, as has his public mourning of Lionel Messi's father, which sparked criticism for its perceived insensitivity. His administration's focus on re-election in 2027 and internal conflicts within La Libertad Avanza further amplify his prominence in the news cycle.

actors.name: Giorgia Meloni
actors.role: Prime Minister of Italy, Leader of Fratelli d'Italia
actors.blurb: Giorgia Meloni continues to shape the European far-right narrative through her hardline stance on immigration and diplomatic tensions with Spain. Over the past 48 hours, her government's refusal to lift Schengen border controls in response to the Ceuta migrant crisis has escalated into a full-blown diplomatic row with Spain, which retaliated by imposing reciprocal border checks. Meloni's vacation in Sardinia and her participation in the 70th anniversary of the Marcinelle mining disaster have also generated significant coverage, particularly her condemnation of CGIL union members for allegedly disrespecting the ceremony. Her leadership within the EU and her party's internal dynamics remain central to her prominence in the news cycle.
